newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs catch up with Bunds, eye France.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs catch up with Bunds, eye France.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds were hit on Thursday by the fall-out of Bunds' slide a day earlier but dealers said the OLO/Bund spread was at the bottom of its range.
The spread, which had narrowed to five from nine basis points on Wednesday, was back at eight basis points.
Belgium often lags a Bund futures selloff in bear markets.
"Yesterday we withstood the pressure very well," one trader said. But the biggest surprise to dealers had been the spread's resilience to the OLO exchange auction on Tuesday.
"Normally that widens the spread but now it didn't lose anything," he said.
Traders said that the market was braced for further weakness but said that elections in France might pose a bigger threat.
"France is performing extremely strongly. It looks as if there are no worries about the elections," one said.
"But if the socialists get more votes than expected, it would do no good to Chirac...and to EMU," he said.
Business was cautious and concentrated in the eight to 10-year zone. The OLO yield curve, which had been flattening last week, was now steepening again, traders said.
